# OKIN Smart Sleep

**Status:** ❓ Needs testing (source-proven BLE bed controls; hardware UNVERIFIED)

**Credit:** Reverse engineering by [kristofferR](https://github.com/kristofferR/ha-adjustable-bed)

## Known Models

The numeric model is an app selector, not proof of physical actuator count.
P1 accepts all models below and an unknown fallback. P2 advertisements force
model 80. Models 3 and 67 share a label and remain distinct.

## Features

| Feature | P1 | P2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Motor Control | Five app controls | Five app controls |
| Position Feedback | None | None |
| Presets | Seven; model 8 uses AI-zero group | Seven |
| Memory Presets | Two recalls; no proven SAVE | Two recalls, six named preset SAVEs |
| Massage | All/off, wave, timer and strength cycles | All/off, cycles and finite catalogs |
| Lights | Toggle | On/off, toggle and read-only brightness |
| Alarm / clock | Weekly/raw mask, five actions, model 67 flexible wake | Weekly/raw mask, nine actions and original app labels |
| Shared settings | Privacy, antisnore, sensitivity, local child mode | Same shared bed channel |

## Choosing a profile

Choose **OKIN Smart Sleep** explicitly when adding the app manually.
Advertisements containing case-sensitive `SLEEP` or `Sleep` and manufacturer
key 89 can select it automatically. Known receiver/service identities retain
precedence. The shared Nordic UART service alone cannot identify this app.

For a payload of at least seven bytes, original byte 6 bit 7 selects P2;
the separate model getter uses byte 6 plus one, with P2 forced to 80.
The app identifier reverses the whole payload and takes bytes 1 through 6.
A short payload uses the lowercase MAC without colons and unknown model.
Home Assistant retains the actual Bluetooth address as its transport identity.

Setup asks for the format and numeric model. These settings belong to each
physical side of a two-address pair. Single-address side routing is unsupported.
The five app labels are HEAD, FOOT, HEADREST (machinery 3), LUMBAR
(machinery 4) and HIPS (machinery 5). They do not establish five fitted motors.

### Aliases

None. Neither format aliases another app or controller.

| Protocol string | 180A | 00002a27-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb | Read |
<!-- /generated -->

Connection attempts use the app's five-second timeout.
The Android app requests MTU 512 after 350 ms. Bleak and Bluetooth proxies
negotiate MTU themselves; all retained writes fit the default 20-byte ATT
payload. No app-level PIN, bond challenge or authentication token is proven.
The P2 initialization remains an opaque session frame.

### Framing and checksum

P1 motor/preset keys use the shared Keeson `p2_side` carrier: a five-byte
payload after its two-byte header. P1 settings have independent shapes.
P2 uses command-specific AA/2A frames, little-endian motor masks and no
checksum. Do not interpret the length-looking fields as a universal envelope.

P1 alarm fields are week/action/hour/minute, with a trailing flexible-wake
boolean. That boolean is not a side selector. P2 has nine wire actions;
the five `app_*` options preserve the original UI mismatch: its ordinal zero
wraps to action 9, and ordinals 1 through 4 emit actions 1 through 4.
The explicit action names address the nine catalog entries directly.

Both formats carry local wall-clock time. P1 uses year minus 1900, zero-based
month and Monday-zero weekday. P2 uses year minus 2000, one-based month and
Monday-one weekday. The action accepts exact byte masks when reproducing an
app schedule; P2's weekday bit is `2**((isoweekday + 1) % 7)`.
No-repeat mask 128 is retained for a future scheduled time; a past scheduled
time replaces it with that date's weekday bit.

### Responses

A complete legacy settings reply supplies massage, sensitivity, antisnore and
privacy. The legacy displayed massage state is active only when timer > 0;
otherwise wave, head, foot and timer display clear. Positive timers clamp the
page timer index to 2. The raw head/foot maximum is log-only and is not a sensor.

Privacy interpretation separately requires protocol string `SENSOR_VOICE` or
`SLEEPVOICE`, with firmware newer than 1.0. That branch reads byte 19 bit 1;
the other branch tests byte 18 equal to 1. The advertisement format bit is
unrelated to this compatibility check.

Legacy alarm replies retain the app's week projection and flexible wake.
P2 light replies carry raw state and brightness; displayed on requires both
nonzero, while toggle follows raw state. Brightness is read-only.
P2 massage replies decode head/foot, mode and remaining timer category.
P2 alarm replies require all 13 bytes even when disabled; complete disable
retains the last schedule. Invalid times and truncated replies publish nothing.
AI-zero status/score retain source names without a physical success claim.

Bed-only framing supports fragments and coalesced complete replies. Partials
expire after one second, reset on a fresh header and never cross sessions.
Sleep/vitals/history notifications do not become position or bed-state data.

### STOP and release behavior

Movement streams at the profile cadence. An ordinary press uses the configured
pulse count; a renewable hold continues until release, lease expiry or the
hold ceiling. Cleanup captures the admitted frame and connection, uses a
fresh cancellation event and drains before the command lock is released.
P2 motor release differs from global STOP. Home Assistant safety STOP bypasses
local child admission, including after child mode changes during a command.

The Android legacy delayed mutable STOP race and uncancelled receive
subscriptions are not reproduced. Stale callbacks, fragments and notifications
from replaced clients are rejected; explicit cleanup disables notifications.

### Vectors

`tests/fixtures/smart_sleep_vectors.json` preserves all 126 original IDs, inputs
and byte strings. `tests/test_smart_sleep_vectors.py` compares all 122 in-scope
literals/formulas and verifies the shared carrier. The remaining four vectors
are excluded history/diagnostic evidence and are not exposed actions.

## Profiles

### P1 legacy

Movement and recall refresh while held and release after the profile delay.
AI-zero sends its duplicate at the query interval. Legacy long-press memory
has no distinct source-proven SAVE and is not advertised as programming.
Massage controls release with global STOP and refresh settings.
Light press requests STOP before its one toggle. Shared privacy/antisnore
settings query status afterward; sensitivity has no invented range or query.
The settings path sends immediate status and its delayed refresh; alarm edits
send the legacy clock after the query delay and refresh the alarm.

### P2 new format

Subscribe before sending opaque initialization. Shared settings still use
the P1 bed channel. Massage and alarm queries use P2.
Arrow release uses motor neutral. Preset release requests global STOP then
recall; a bounded 5.5-second preset gesture can send its separate SAVE.
Flat has no SAVE. Direct save buttons and memory programming send the same
proven SAVE frames. The card exposes P2 presets as ordinary recall buttons, with explicit SAVE
actions. The bounded preset gesture remains available through the hold action;
cancelled HA gestures clean up without starting a new recall.

Local child mode is a Home Assistant admission setting, persisted across
restarts. It is not a hardware lock or authentication claim. It gates movement,
presets and P2 custom controls; shared legacy settings remain usable.

## Notes

Wi-Fi, accounts/cloud, OTA, historical reports, sleep/vitals analytics,
phone media, WebView, diagnostics and unrelated accessory consumers are outside
the BLE bed boundary. Wi-Fi-named models retain their proven bed controls.
No physical motor-position, calibration, RGB setter or concurrent side protocol
is established by this artifact.

- OKIN Smart Sleep 2.4.9 (263), package `com.bedding.monitor.sleep_monitor.release`.
- XAPK SHA-256: `92e4bc4925494f66ef820cf5cdd334b2faba4443c800e664658d7165af0eb4c6`.
- Accepted APK Protocol Audit row094, including scoped A1-A4 repairs.
- Hardware remains UNVERIFIED. External beta/release users may validate physical
  actuator labels, STOP/SAVE effects, alarm label behavior and both formats.

Legacy P1 weekly schedules use `week_mask` directly; the P2 weekday conversion
is not inferred for legacy masks. Supplying P1 `weekdays` without an exact
mask is rejected before writing.
